thread:
anya: Quick heads-up — canary run for quantized-sablex-lite (int8 streaming) shows intermittent funcall output that fails our schema-lint. Repro sample attached. Looks correlated with KV-prefixing and short prompt batches.

sam: Ugh. Do you have a failing output example?

anya: Yep:```
{
  "tool": "search",
  "args": {
    "q": "latest quarterly metrics"
  }
}

--extra\u0000
```
Trailing garbage \u0000 after the JSON. Parser rejects it. This only shows up when run through the streaming path with kvcache enabled.

taylor: Thanks. Is this the streaming NDJSON path or the chunked funcall stream?

anya: Chunked funcall stream from the runtime (we stream structured output tokens). The model emits valid JSON then adds a tiny null byte plus a newline in ~1/80 samples.

mike: That smells like a tokenizer/control-char issue introduced during quantization kernel changes. Could be a postprocess concat bug too. Did the canary run on int8-only replicas?

anya: Yes int8 canary set. Mirror runs on float16 don't show it.

eva: @taylor can you pull the kvcache prefixing codepath? Maybe the prefix buffer adds a control sentinel when concatenating cached tokens.

canary-bot: canary-job-1739512468 launched on sandbox-int8-02 at 11:04 UTC. Metrics: parse_fail_rate=1.2% (baseline 0.02%).

sam: Quick triage idea: add a lightweight post-emit sanitizer that strips trailing \u0000 and printable-control-chars before schema-lint. Not a fix but reduces customer impact.

taylor: Agreed for short-term. For root-cause we need: (1) raw token stream capture for failing cases (no postprocessing), (2) compare token -> byte mapping on int8 vs fp16, (3) run with kvcache off to confirm correlation.

anya: I started a dump job for five failing IDs (attached). I'm also running a mirror with kvcache disabled.

mike: Add a small fuzz harness that injects boundary cases around EOS and prefix boundaries; we can surface if tokenization or kernel emit is responsible.

eva: Also please check the runtime's chunk-assembly code: when we merge streaming fragments we use `bytearray.extend(...)` on preserved buffers — if a null sentinel was used for alignment earlier it could leak.

sam: If we do the sanitizer route, let's make it opt-in per-customer + opt-out for canaries to keep signal. Can we also emit a telemetry tag for "postemit_sanitized"?

anya: Will do. For this canary I've enabled the sanitizer locally and parse_fail_rate dropped to 0.04% (still slightly above baseline).

taylor: Nice. Can you paste the raw failing token hex sequence?

anya: Sure:
```
... 0x7b 0x22 0x74 0x6f 0x6f 0x6c 0x22 0x3a 0x22 0x73 0x65 0x61 0x72 0x63 0x68 0x22 0x2c 0x22 0x61 0x72 0x67 0x73 0x22 0x3a 0x7b 0x22 0x71 0x22 0x3a 0x22 0x6d 0x65 0x74 0x72 0x69 0x63 0x73 0x22 0x7d 0x7d 0x0a 0x00 0x0a
...
```

mike: That 0x00 followed by 0x0a is suspicious. If the tokenizer outputs a raw 0x00 token mapping when using an optimized kernel, it could be a bug in the byte-to-token mapping table used by the int8 kernel.

eva: Low-cost repro: run the streaming canary with sequence_length small (<=64) and artificially pad kvcache with short prefixes. If rate goes up, we triage kernel.

anya: Running that now. ETA ~12m. Also adding a temp lint rule: fail only if trailing non-whitespace non-control bytes exist after JSON; treat control chars \u0000 as sanitizable.

canary-bot: canary-job-1739512468/kvcache-off launched on sandbox-int8-03 at 11:12 UTC.

taylor: If kvcache-off run passes, schedule a bisect over recent runtime kernel commits (last 3) and the quantization microcode. Prioritize any commit that touched token-maps or chunk-assembly.

sam: I can run the bisect tomorrow morning; leave notes in the runbook section. Also we should add a unit test in the struct-output harness that simulates trailing nulls so future regressions fail CI.

anya: Results: kvcache-off parse_fail_rate now 0.01%. That nails correlation.

mike: Great. Next steps: (1) add sanitizer fallback and telemetry (anya), (2) add unit+fuzz tests in runtime repo (mike), (3) bisect quant kernel/token-map (sam), (4) postmortem doc if kernel change is root cause (taylor).

eva: I'll open a short PR to make the chunk-assembly defensive (trim \u0000 at fragment boundaries) with a feature flag.

anya: Thanks all — I'll push the sanitizer PR and the failing case dump. Filing an internal ticket: ML-ONBOARD-1862.

sam: Thanks. If anyone wants to pair on the bisect ping me. :thumbsup:

mike: Adding the unit test now. Will link to ML-ONBOARD-1862.

taylor: Good work. Let's aim to close the canary loop and roll int8 back to stable only after we have a kernel patch and the new tests.

anya: Agreed. Will keep updates here.
